Name: Liqun Luo
Keywords: TRAP2; activity-dependent labeling; genetic access; neuronal ensembles; memory retrieval
Summary: Characterized TRAP2, an improved activity-dependent labeling/access tool in mice, and connected changing prelimbic cortical ensembles with remote fear-memory retrieval.
Attribution: Luo coauthored the study with Laura A. DeNardo and colleagues. The paper credits DeNardo and Luo with study design and manuscript preparation, and DeNardo with TRAP2 characterization.
Source_title: Temporal evolution of cortical ensembles promoting remote memory retrieval.
Supports: The 2019 DeNardo et al. paper explicitly describes detailed TRAP2 characterization and its memory-ensemble application, with the specified author-contribution statement.
Note: 2019 is the detailed-characterization publication, not an asserted invention or first-disclosure date. The paper cites Allen et al. 2017 for prior TRAP2 development and Guenthner et al. 2013 for original TRAP; TRAP and TRAP2 are not interchangeable.

Name: Liqun Luo
Keywords: teneurin; synaptic partner matching; wiring specificity; olfactory circuits; Ten-m; Ten-a
Summary: Identified Ten-m and Ten-a as molecules instructing matching between selected olfactory receptor neurons and projection neurons in Drosophila, with evidence supporting homophilic recognition.
Attribution: Luo coauthored the study with Weizhe Hong and Timothy J. Mosca.
Source_title: Teneurins instruct synaptic partner matching in an olfactory map.
Supports: The 2012 Hong, Mosca, and Luo paper reports the Ten-m/Ten-a matching result in the Drosophila olfactory circuit.
Note: A bounded circuit-specific finding, not a claim that one molecule or investigator explains all synaptic specificity.

Name: Karel Svoboda
Contribution: ALM persistent/preparatory activity for motor planning
Keywords: ALM; motor planning; persistent activity; preparatory activity; robust neural dynamics; interhemispheric coupling
Summary: Linked movement-selective preparatory activity in mouse anterior lateral motor cortex to upcoming movement and its transformation into movement commands. Follow-up work showed recovery after unilateral disruption, supporting interacting hemispheres in robust motor planning.
Attribution: Svoboda coauthored the 2015 study with Nuo Li, Tsai-Wen Chen, Zengcai V. Guo, and Charles R. Gerfen, and the 2016 study with Nuo Li, Kayvon Daie, and Shaul Druckmann. These are collaborative contributions, not sole-discovery claims.
Source_title: A motor cortex circuit for motor planning and movement.
Supports: The 2015 Li et al. paper names Svoboda as a coauthor and links mouse ALM preparatory activity, projection-neuron classes, and movement commands.
Note: The displayed year identifies the 2015 anchor; the second linked anchor is from 2016. This selected contribution family is not an exhaustive history or a priority claim for all motor-planning research.
